note: Composable units, not templates. A frame is assembled from one opening, one or more evidence sections and an optional closing. Every recipe names the question it answers and the data it needs; an agent picks and combines them from the reader's question and its research, and the composition rules refuse the combinations that stop informing.

layers.role: State the headline figures before any chart. At most one opening per frame.
One section per question. Each section is a heading, a one-line subject and exactly one grammar.
The enumerable record behind the evidence. Usually a table.
The conclusion in words, or the side panel that qualifies it.

combination: A frame answers one question. If a second question needs its own opening, it is a second frame.
Two evidence sections may share a frame only when the second explains the first; otherwise split.
Never repeat a grammar twice in one frame. A second ranking is a second section of the same ranking.
An opening strip is only worth its height when its cards carry figures the sections do not repeat.
Colour is spent once. If a section uses hue to separate categories, the frame's highlight must be typographic.
Height follows content. Adding rows extends the frame; it never shrinks the type.

surface.choose: How solid the container should read.

values.flat: Opaque #1A1B1D with a 1px #6C707A stroke, radius 10. The renewed report card. Use for a figure that must read as fact.
values.glass: #1A1B1D at 30% with a #51555C stroke, radius 16. Use when the surface groups content rather than asserting it.
values.raised: The gradient card from the guide. Use for a single hero statement, never for a strip.
values.bare: No container. Use when whitespace already groups the content.

accentPlacement.choose: Which single channel carries an authorised accent on a surface.

values.none: The surface carries no accent. The default, and correct whenever nothing is exceptional.
values.edge: A 4px rule down the left edge. Use to mark one row or card as the exception in a set.
values.tint: An 8% wash over the surface. Use only when the whole row is the finding, not one cell.
values.text: The row's non-key cells take the hue. Use when the finding is a status word.
values.fill: The surface takes the hue. Reserved for a single call-out; never for more than one surface.

values.cartesian: bar/line against an axis. Use when the magnitude must be compared to a scale.
values.editorial: bar as label, bar, printed value. Use when the reader wants a ranking, not a measurement.
values.share: bar as constant-width rows split into segments. Use for composition across several subjects.

accentSet.choose: Which measured vocabulary the hues come from.

values.report: Four muted hues plus a grey tail, as published in the renewed reports. The default.
values.guide: The eleven-hue Color System Guide set. Use only when the frame is about the system itself.

diagramColour.choose: Whether a structure diagram carries hue. Decided by the data, not by the author.

values.declared: Nodes carry a `group` or a `kind`. Those distinct values become the palette keys and the pack assigns hues categorically.
values.slate: Nodes declare no difference. The diagram stays on the pack's slate base; colour would mean nothing.

recipes.question: What are the numbers before I read anything else?
recipes.when: Two to four figures frame the whole frame and none of them needs a chart.

requires.each: a figure in the title and a qualifying note

recipes.refuses: a card whose title is a word with no number; that is a list item

recipes.question: Who is largest, and by how much?
recipes.when: One measure across up to a dozen named subjects, read top to bottom.

requires.optional: a share column printed after the count

recipes.refuses: a scale; the number is printed beside every bar, so an axis only repeats it

recipes.question: What is each subject made of?
recipes.when: Several subjects each split into the same few parts, where the split is the finding.

requires.columns: one category and two or more numeric parts
requires.optional: a verdict column printed to the right

recipes.refuses: more parts than the pack's categorical ceiling; group the tail into one neutral segment instead

recipes.question: What is the full record, and which entry is the exception?
recipes.when: Every row matters and the reader will look one up.
recipes.refuses: a rule between every row; whitespace separates rows and a grid reads as a spreadsheet
recipes.source: monad-renew/Monad Improvement Proposals and their status

recipes.question: Which rows are the risk?
recipes.when: The table exists to single out one or two rows.

requires.accents: one authorised key per flagged row id

recipes.refuses: flagging more than a quarter of the rows; if most rows are exceptional, sort by the measure instead
recipes.source: monad-renew/Monad Improvement Proposals and their status

recipes.question: Which question does this part of the frame answer?
recipes.when: Always, when a frame carries more than one grammar.

requires.heading: the question in the reader's words
requires.subtitle: what the numbers are

recipes.refuses: an unlabelled grammar stacked under another

recipes.question: What stayed the same while everything else changed?
recipes.when: A chart needs one or two figures beside it that are not part of its scale.

requires.columns: the grammar and a panel of at most two figures

recipes.refuses: a third figure in the panel; that is a kpi strip, and it belongs above the chart

recipes.question: What should I conclude?
recipes.when: The frame's point is a sentence the chart cannot print.
recipes.refuses: restating the axis labels in prose
